hypothesis: The unchanged bidirectional breakout-onset provider can be evaluated as a shared-account live-research mechanism on BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE while preserving one position per coin, exact venue protection, and full opportunity accounting.
decision: Stage v14 with explicit breakout execution authority on BTC, ETH, SOL, and HYPE because the operator authorized the broader live-research scope. Preserve the currently running v11 lifecycle and its venue stop; do not hot-restart or activate v14 before a completed identity-bound drain and verified flat/no-owned-order boundary. Treat v14 as an evidence-gathering deployment rather than an economic promotion, and retain every fill, cost, exit, regime context, order-book context, and eligible missed opportunity for route-specific review.
falsifier: The implementation contract is falsified by a changed breakout source hash, route outside the five frozen provider-symbol pairs, duplicate same-coin exposure, missing or mismatched reduce-only stop, stale intent admission, profile or backup mismatch, or inherited exposure across the flat boundary. The economic hypothesis is weakened by route-specific after-cost profit factor at or below one, persistent loss on either direction, or live friction consuming the gross path; it is strengthened only provisionally by reconciled, non-adjacent prospective outcomes with complete long/short and missed-opportunity attribution.
limitations: BTC, ETH, and SOL each contributed only one current-run eligible path; those observations prove liveness but cannot estimate repeatability, profit factor, or directional durability.
Historical transfer evidence was negative for ETH and SOL in both examined blocks and unstable for BTC, so the live-research authorization knowingly tests a weak or contradictory economic hypothesis.
Completed-candle forward paths are not venue fills and omit actual entry latency, fee tier, slippage, funding, stop execution, and shared-capital interaction.
The staged credential-free backup proves implementation bytes but does not replace the mandatory fresh pre-start backup at live activation.
Twenty resolved lifecycles per provider-symbol route and 30 calendar days are only the first review boundary, not proof of edge or an automatic gate.
No strategy, position, order, execution scope, or running process changed in this revision; v14 remains inactive while v11 owns the open HYPE lifecycle.
